question: In Mendel's experiment, what did he observe in the F1 generation when he crossed a tall (TT) and a short (tt) pea plant?
option_4: Half were tall, half was short
solution_text:
The correct answer is All were tall.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When Mendel crossed a pure tall (TT) pea plant with a pure short (tt) pea plant, all the plants of the F1 generation were tall.

 

• This happens because tallness is the dominant trait and shortness is the recessive trait. Every F1 plant has the genotype Tt, and since T dominates over t, the dominant character (tall) alone is expressed.

 

• This observation led Mendel to formulate the Law of Dominance, which states that when two contrasting alleles are present together, only the dominant allele expresses itself in the phenotype, while the recessive allele remains hidden.

 

• When these F1 (Tt) plants are self-pollinated, the F2 generation shows a 3:1 phenotypic ratio of tall to short plants, revealing that the recessive trait reappears.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mendel conducted his experiments on the garden pea (Pisum sativum) because it has easily distinguishable contrasting traits, is self-pollinating, and produces a large number of offspring in a short time.

 

• The genotypic ratio in F2 for a monohybrid cross is 1 (TT) : 2 (Tt) : 1 (tt), while the phenotypic ratio is 3 (tall) : 1 (short).

 

NOTE

 

• All were short (Option A): Incorrect — this would only happen if shortness were dominant, which is not the case here.

 

• All were medium height (Option B): Incorrect — Mendel's traits show complete dominance, not blending, so no intermediate form appears.

 

• Half were tall, half was short (Option D): This 1:1 ratio actually describes a test cross (Tt × tt), not the F1 of a TT × tt cross.

question: Which one of the following is an advantage of vegetative propagation in flowering plants?
option_1: They can flower and fruit later than those produced by seeds.
option_2: They can flower and fruit earlier than those produced by seeds.
option_3: They are completely different from their parent plants.
option_4: They can show completely new characters than those produced by seeds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They can flower and fruit earlier than those produced by seeds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction in which new plants grow from vegetative parts such as roots, stems or leaves (e.g., cuttings, grafting, layering, tubers).

 

• Since plants raised through vegetative propagation are grown from an already mature part of the parent plant, they flower and bear fruit earlier than plants grown from seeds, which must first pass through a long juvenile growth stage.

 

• Vegetatively propagated plants are genetically identical to the parent plant (clones), which is useful for preserving desirable characteristics such as seedless fruits (banana, orange) or a particular flower colour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common methods of artificial vegetative propagation include cutting (rose, sugarcane), layering (jasmine, strawberry) and grafting (mango, apple).

 

• Natural vegetative propagation occurs through structures like rhizomes (ginger), tubers (potato), bulbs (onion) and runners (grass).

 

NOTE

 

• They flower and fruit later (Option A): Incorrect — it is the opposite; vegetative propagation speeds up flowering/fruiting.

 

• Completely different from parent (Option C) and Show completely new characters (Option D): Both are incorrect, since vegetatively propagated plants are clones and are genetically identical to the parent, not different.

question: Which organelle is called the 'suicidal bag' of the cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lysosome.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles containing powerful digestive (hydrolytic) enzymes capable of breaking down proteins, lipids, carbohydrates and nucleic acids.

 

• They are called the 'suicidal bags' of the cell because when the cell is damaged or dies, the lysosomal membrane may rupture and release these enzymes, which then digest the cell's own components (autolysis).

 

• Lysosomes also perform useful roles in a healthy cell, such as digesting worn-out organelles, foreign particles and pathogens engulfed by the cell.

 

• They are formed by the Golgi apparatus and were discovered by Christian de Duve.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mitochondria are called the 'powerhouse of the cell' since they generate ATP through cellular respiration.

 

• The Golgi body is called the 'packaging and dispatching unit' of the cell, as it modifies, sorts and packages proteins for secretion.

 

• Ribosomes are the 'protein factories' of the cell, being the site of protein synthesis.

 

NOTE

 

• Ribosome (Option A): Site of protein synthesis; not membrane-bound.

 

• Golgi body (Option B): Involved in packaging and secretion, not digestion of the cell itself.

 

• Mitochondria (Option C): Site of aerobic respiration and ATP generation.

question: What is the purpose of a plug key in an electrical circuit?
option_1: It measures the potential difference in a circuit.
option_2: It provides potential difference in a circuit.
option_3: It helps in connecting and disconnecting a circuit.
option_4: It measures the current flowing through a circuit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It helps in connecting and disconnecting a circuit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A plug key (switch) is a simple device inserted into an electric circuit that allows the circuit to be completed (closed) or broken (opened) at will.

 

• When the key is inserted/closed, the circuit becomes complete and current flows; when it is removed/opened, the circuit breaks and current stops flowing.

 

• It is a basic safety and control component and does not by itself measure or provide anything — it only controls the flow path.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• A voltmeter measures potential difference and is always connected in parallel across a component.

 

• An ammeter measures current and is always connected in series in the circuit.

 

• A cell/battery provides the potential difference (EMF) that drives the current in a circuit.

 

NOTE

 

• Option A describes a voltmeter, not a plug key.

 

• Option B describes a source of EMF such as a cell or battery.

 

• Option D describes an ammeter.

question: A person pushes a massive, stationary object (like a parked truck) with force F. The object pushes back with force −F. Why does the object NOT accelerate if the reaction force is equal and opposite, as suggested by the Third Law?
option_1: The net force on the object is zero because the action and reaction forces cancel out.
option_2: The magnitude of the force F is insufficient to overcome the object's inherent potential energy.
option_3: The forces act instantaneously, preventing momentum change.
option_4: The action and reaction forces act on different objects, but the static friction on the stationary object balances the applied push force F.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The action and reaction forces act on different objects, but the static friction on the stationary object balances the applied push force F.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Newton's Third Law of Motion states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, but this action-reaction pair acts on two different bodies (the person and the truck), so the two forces can never cancel each other for a single body.

 

• The truck does not move because the only forces acting on the truck itself are the push F (from the person) and the static friction force from the ground, which automatically adjusts up to its maximum value to oppose relative motion and balances F, keeping the net force on the truck zero.

 

• Since the net force on the truck is zero, by Newton's Second Law (F = ma), its acceleration is zero, and it remains stationary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Static friction is a self-adjusting force that increases with the applied force up to a maximum limit called limiting friction; beyond this the object begins to move and kinetic friction takes over.

 

• Newton's laws of motion: First Law (Inertia), Second Law (F = ma), Third Law (action-reaction) — all formulated by Sir Isaac Newton in his 1687 work *Principia Mathematica*.

 

NOTE

 

• Option A wrongly applies the action-reaction pair (which acts on two different bodies) to a single body's net force — a very common misconception.

 

• Option B is not a real physical explanation; 'potential energy' has nothing to do with this scenario.

 

• Option C is meaningless; forces don't act 'instantaneously' in this special sense — momentum change depends on net force and time, not on any such property.

question:
Which of the following statements are NOT true regarding the principal axis of a spherical mirror?

(i) It is an imaginary straight line passing through the pole and the centre of curvature of a spherical mirror.

(ii) Principal axis is normal to the mirror at its pole.

(iii) A ray parallel to the principal axis after reflection from the mirror passes through the centre of curvature of the mirror.

(iv) The focus of a spherical mirror does not lie on its principal axis.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both (iii) and (iv).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement (i) is TRUE: The principal axis is indeed the imaginary straight line joining the pole (P) and the centre of curvature (C) of the spherical mirror.

 

• Statement (ii) is TRUE: The principal axis is perpendicular (normal) to the mirror's surface at the pole.

 

• Statement (iii) is FALSE: A ray parallel to the principal axis, after reflection, passes through the principal focus (F), not the centre of curvature. Only a ray passing through/directed towards the centre of curvature retraces its own path.

 

• Statement (iv) is FALSE: The focus lies ON the principal axis, exactly midway between the pole and the centre of curvature (F = R/2, where R is the radius of curvature).

 

• Since (iii) and (iv) are the incorrect statements, they are the ones that are NOT true.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rules for ray diagrams in spherical mirrors: a ray parallel to the principal axis reflects through F; a ray through F reflects parallel to the axis; a ray through C retraces its path; a ray hitting the pole reflects at an equal angle to the axis.

 

• Relation between focal length and radius of curvature: f = R/2.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A, B and D incorrectly include one or both of the genuinely true statements (i) and (ii), or omit one of the genuinely false statements.

question: As Newton is to weight, ___________ is to pressure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pascal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Weight is a force, and the SI unit of force is the Newton (N).

 

• Similarly, pressure is force per unit area, and its SI unit is the Pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

 

• This question tests a simple analogy: just as Newton is the SI unit used to measure weight (a force), Pascal is the SI unit used to measure pressure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kilogram (kg) is the SI unit of mass, not weight — weight is mass × acceleration due to gravity (W = mg), measured in Newtons.

 

• Kilogram per cubic metre (kg/m³) is the SI unit of density.

 

• Kelvin (K) is the SI unit of temperature.

 

• Other common units of pressure include atmosphere (atm), bar and torr/mm of Hg; 1 atm ≈ 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa.

 

NOTE

 

• Kilogram (Option B): Measures mass, a base quantity, not weight (which is a force) or pressure.

 

• Kilogram per cubic metre (Option A): Unit of density.

 

• Kelvin (Option C): Unit of temperature.

question: Which of the following metallic oxides can be reduced to metals by heating alone?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mercuric oxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Metals that lie very low in the reactivity series (such as mercury and silver) form oxides that are thermally unstable and decompose into the free metal and oxygen merely on heating, without needing a separate reducing agent.

 

• Mercuric oxide (HgO), when heated, decomposes to give mercury metal and oxygen gas: 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂. This is a classic example used to demonstrate thermal decomposition in chemistry.

 

• Metals that are more reactive (like zinc, iron, manganese) form oxides that are thermally stable and require an external reducing agent such as carbon, hydrogen or a more reactive metal to be reduced to the free metal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The reactivity series (in decreasing order): K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag, Au. Metals at the bottom (Hg, Ag, Au) are the least reactive and their oxides decompose on heating alone.

 

• Zinc oxide (ZnO) is reduced to zinc using carbon (ZnO + C → Zn + CO), a process called smelting.

 

• Iron (III) oxide (Fe₂O₃) is reduced using carbon monoxide/coke in a blast furnace.

 

NOTE

 

• Zinc oxide (Option A), Iron (III) oxide (Option B) and Manganese oxide (Option D) are all thermally stable oxides of moderately reactive metals and need an external reducing agent, not heat alone.

question: How does the sound of a patient's heartbeat travel from the chest piece to the doctor's ear through a stethoscope?
solution_text:
The correct answer is By multiple reflection of sound.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A simple (acoustic, non-electronic) stethoscope works on the principle of the multiple (repeated) reflection of sound through its hollow tube.

 

• Sound produced by the heartbeat travels through the flexible tube of the stethoscope by getting reflected again and again off the inner walls of the tube, so almost no sound energy escapes and it reaches the doctor's ear undiminished in intensity.

 

• This is analogous to how sound travels through a hollow pipe or megaphone, both applications of the law of reflection of sound.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other everyday applications of the reflection of sound include SONAR (used to find the depth of the sea/detect submarines), the megaphone/loudhailer, and the curved ceilings of concert halls designed to focus sound onto the audience.

 

• Electronic stethoscopes do convert sound to electrical signals for amplification, but the classical/basic acoustic stethoscope relies purely on the reflection of sound.

 

NOTE

 

• Conversion to electrical signals (Option A): True only for electronic stethoscopes, not the standard/classical one.

 

• Refraction (Option B): Refraction is the bending of sound when it passes from one medium to another with a different density/speed; it is not involved here.

 

• Direct transmission without reflection (Option C): Incorrect — the tube's bends make multiple reflection essential.

question:
Match the common name of the bee with its scientific name.

Column I (Common Name)

1. Indian bee

2. Rock bee

3. Little bee

4. Italian bee

 

Column II (Scientific Name)

A. Apis mellifera

B. Apis cerana indica

C. Apis dorsata

D. Apis florea
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-B, 2-C, 3-D, 4-A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian bee (1) → Apis cerana indica (B): The common domesticated honeybee of India, widely reared for honey production.

 

• Rock bee (2) → Apis dorsata (C): The largest of the Indian honeybees; builds a single large exposed comb, usually on high rocks, tall trees or buildings, and is known for being highly aggressive.

 

• Little bee (3) → Apis florea (D): The smallest honeybee species found in India; builds small, exposed combs on bushes and hedges and gives comparatively little honey.

 

• Italian bee (4) → Apis mellifera (A): A European species introduced into India for commercial beekeeping because of its high honey yield and gentle nature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Apiculture is the scientific term for beekeeping/honey cultivation.

 

• Honeybees live in a highly organised social colony consisting of one queen, several hundred drones (males), and thousands of worker bees.

 

NOTE

 

• The remaining options (B, C, D) mismatch one or more common names with the wrong scientific name, so they are incorrect.

question: Work done by a force is said to be positive when:
option_1: the force has a component in the direction of displacement
option_2: the angle between force and displacement is 90°
option_3: the force opposes the motion of the body
option_4: the displacement of the body is zero
solution_text:
The correct answer is the force has a component in the direction of displacement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Work done is defined as W = F·d·cosθ, where F is the applied force, d is the displacement, and θ is the angle between the force and the direction of displacement.

 

• Work is positive when the force (or a component of it) acts in the same general direction as the displacement, i.e. when θ is between 0° and 90° (cos θ > 0).

 

• For example, when you push a box and it moves forward, the applied force has a component along the displacement, so positive work is done on the box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Work is zero when the force is perpendicular to the displacement (θ = 90°), e.g. a coolie carrying a load horizontally while the load's weight acts vertically downward — since cos 90° = 0.

 

• Work is negative when the force opposes the displacement (θ between 90° and 180°), e.g. friction acting opposite to motion.

 

• The SI unit of work is the joule (J), where 1 J = 1 N × 1 m.

 

NOTE

 

• Angle 90° (Option B): Gives zero work, not positive work.

 

• Force opposing motion (Option C): Gives negative work.

 

• Zero displacement (Option D): Gives zero work regardless of the force applied.

question: Which process is used to prepare sodium hydroxide from brine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Electrolysis of brine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium hydroxide (NaOH), also called caustic soda, is industrially manufactured by the electrolysis of a concentrated solution of common salt (brine, i.e. aqueous NaCl). This is known as the chlor-alkali process.

 

• On passing electricity through brine: chlorine gas is released at the anode, hydrogen gas at the cathode, and sodium hydroxide solution is left near the cathode.

 

• The overall reaction: 2NaCl + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + Cl₂ + H₂ (electrolysis).

 

• Since useful products (NaOH, Cl₂, H₂) are all obtained from this single process, it is called the chlor-alkali process — 'chlor' for chlorine and 'alkali' for sodium hydroxide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chlorine produced is used to make bleaching powder, PVC and disinfectants; hydrogen is used as fuel and in the manufacture of margarine.

 

• The Solvay process is used to manufacture sodium carbonate (washing soda, Na₂CO₃), not sodium hydroxide.

 

• The Haber process is used industrially to manufacture ammonia (NH₃) from nitrogen and hydrogen.

 

NOTE

 

• Solvay process (Option B): Produces sodium carbonate, a different alkali.

 

• Haber process (Option C): Produces ammonia, unrelated to NaOH.

 

• Thermal decomposition of NaCl (Option D): Not a real industrial method; NaCl is extremely thermally stable and does not decompose this way.

question: Which of the following metals reacts most vigorously with water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium (Na) is a highly reactive alkali metal that reacts violently and vigorously with cold water, releasing hydrogen gas and enough heat to melt itself and often ignite the liberated hydrogen: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂ + heat.

 

• Sodium floats and moves rapidly on the surface of water due to the heat released, sometimes catching fire — this is the classic demonstration of alkali metal reactivity.

 

• Reactivity with water generally follows the reactivity series: metals higher up (like potassium, sodium, calcium) react vigorously even with cold water, while those lower down react slowly (like zinc, iron with steam) or not at all (like gold, silver).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Potassium is even more reactive than sodium and reacts explosively with water.

 

• Calcium reacts with cold water but less vigorously (bubbles of hydrogen form steadily, without catching fire).

 

• Magnesium reacts with hot water/steam; zinc and iron react only with steam; lead, copper, silver and gold do not react with water at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Zinc (Option A) and Iron (Option C): React only with steam, not cold water, and even then only slowly.

 

• Lead (Option B): Does not react with water under normal conditions.

question: The shortest distance between the initial and final positions of an object is called ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is displacement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Displacement is defined as the shortest straight-line distance between the initial position and the final position of a moving object, along with its direction. It is a vector quantity.

 

• Distance, on the other hand, is the total actual path length covered by the object, regardless of direction, and is a scalar quantity. Distance is always greater than or equal to displacement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Speed is the rate of change of distance with time (scalar); velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time (vector).

 

• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.

 

• If a body returns to its starting point, its displacement is zero, but the distance travelled is never zero (as long as it moved).

 

NOTE

 

• Acceleration (Option A): Relates to the rate of change of velocity, not to position.

 

• Speed (Option C): Relates to distance covered per unit time, a scalar, not the shortest path between two points.

 

• Distance (Option D): Refers to the total path length, which can be longer than the shortest straight-line path (displacement).

question: Colloidal particles are separated by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is centrifugation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Colloidal particles are intermediate in size between those of a true solution and a suspension (roughly 1 nm to 1000 nm), so they pass through ordinary filter paper and cannot be separated by simple filtration.

 

• They can, however, be separated from the dispersion medium using centrifugation, in which the mixture is spun at very high speed, and the resulting centrifugal force causes the denser colloidal particles to settle out.

 

• This principle is used in ultracentrifuges to separate colloidal particles like proteins and viruses, and is also the basis of cream separators used to separate cream from milk.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Colloidal particles can also be separated by dialysis (using a semi-permeable membrane) or by the Tyndall effect used to detect (not separate) their presence, since colloids scatter light while true solutions do not.

 

• A true solution has particle size less than 1 nm and passes through both filter paper and a semi-permeable membrane; a suspension has particles larger than 1000 nm and can be separated by ordinary filtration.

 

NOTE

 

• Filtration (Option A): Works for suspensions (large particles), not colloids.

 

• Boiling (Option C) and Recrystallisation (Option D): Used for purifying/separating true solutions or solid compounds, not for separating colloidal dispersions.

question: What is the relationship between the incident ray and the emergent ray after light passes through the two parallel opposite faces of a rectangular glass slab?
option_1: The emergent ray converges to a point on the principal axis
option_2: The emergent ray is parallel to the direction of the incident ray, but shifted sideward slightly
option_3: The emergent ray is reflected back along the path of the incident ray
option_4: The emergent ray is perpendicular to the incident ray
solution_text:
The correct answer is The emergent ray is parallel to the direction of the incident ray, but shifted sideward slightly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When light passes through a rectangular glass slab, it undergoes refraction twice — once while entering (denser medium, ray bends towards the normal) and once while leaving (rarer medium, ray bends away from the normal).

 

• Because the two refracting surfaces of the slab are parallel to each other, the two bendings exactly cancel each other's angular effect, so the emergent ray comes out parallel to the original incident ray.

 

• However, the emergent ray is laterally displaced — shifted sideways from the line of the incident ray — because the light travelled an extra sideways distance while passing through the slab. This offset is called lateral displacement/shift.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lateral displacement depends on the thickness of the slab, the angle of incidence, and the refractive index of the glass — greater thickness or angle of incidence gives a larger shift.

 

• This concept is different from that of a prism, where the two refracting surfaces are inclined (not parallel), so the emergent ray is not parallel to the incident ray but bends towards the base (angle of deviation).

 

NOTE

 

• Converges at a point on principal axis (Option A): This describes the behaviour of a converging lens/mirror, not a plane-faced glass slab.

 

• Reflects back (Option C): This would happen only in the special case of normal incidence with total internal reflection or a mirrored surface, not ordinary refraction through a slab.

 

• Perpendicular to incident ray (Option D): Not correct for a simple parallel-faced slab.

question: Which of the following meristems is responsible for the lengthwise growth at the ends of shoots and roots?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Apical meristem.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Apical meristems are located at the tips (apices) of roots and shoots and are responsible for the plant's increase in length (primary growth).

 

• This growth results in the elongation of the root and shoot, allowing the plant to grow taller and its roots to penetrate deeper into the soil.

 

• Apical meristems give rise to the primary permanent tissues of the plant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Intercalary meristem is present at the base of leaves or internodes (e.g. in grasses) and is responsible for the regrowth of grass after cutting/grazing.

 

• Lateral meristem (cambium) occurs on the sides of stems and roots and is responsible for increase in girth (thickness), i.e. secondary growth.

 

• 'Permanent meristem' is not a standard type; once meristematic cells differentiate, they are called permanent tissue (which does not divide further).

 

NOTE

 

• Intercalary meristem (Option B): Responsible for regrowth after cutting, not for the primary lengthwise growth at the tips.

 

• Lateral meristem (Option C): Responsible for growth in thickness (girth), not length.

 

• Permanent meristem (Option D): Not a genuine meristem type — permanent tissue does not actively divide.

question: At higher levels of the atmosphere, which of the following shields the surface of the earth from ultraviolet radiation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ozone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ozone layer (O₃) is found in the stratosphere (roughly 15–35 km above the earth's surface) and absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation coming from the sun, preventing it from reaching the earth's surface.

 

• Without this protective ozone shield, high UV exposure would cause serious harm to living organisms, including skin cancer, cataracts and damage to plant life.

 

• Ozone depletion, largely caused by chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), has led to the formation of the 'ozone hole', most prominently over Antarctica.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Montreal Protocol (1987) is an international treaty to phase out substances responsible for ozone depletion; World Ozone Day is observed on 16 September.

 

• Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere and is essential for proteins/DNA but does not absorb UV radiation.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrogen (Option A): The most abundant atmospheric gas, but not involved in UV shielding.

 

• Hydrogen (Option B) and Carbon (Option D): Neither is a significant/relevant component of the atmosphere in this context.

question: How is molecular mass calculated?
option_1: Adding all atomic volumes of the atoms present
option_2: Adding all atomic masses of the atoms in molecule
option_3: By squaring atomic numbers of all elements
option_4: Multiplying atomic radii of constituent elements
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adding all atomic masses of the atoms in molecule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The molecular mass (molecular weight) of a substance is calculated by adding together the atomic masses of all the atoms present in one molecule of that substance, taking into account the number of each type of atom.

 

• For example, the molecular mass of water (H₂O) = 2 × (atomic mass of H) + 1 × (atomic mass of O) = 2×1 + 16 = 18 u.

 

• Molecular mass is expressed in atomic mass units (u) or daltons, referenced to 1/12th the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Formula mass is used for ionic compounds (which don't exist as discrete molecules) and is calculated the same way, using the empirical formula.

 

• Gram molecular mass is the molecular mass expressed in grams and equals the mass of one mole of the substance.

 

NOTE

 

• Adding atomic volumes (Option A), squaring atomic numbers (Option C) and multiplying atomic radii (Option D) are all fabricated definitions with no basis in actual chemistry.

question: Which of the following correctly describes how potential difference between two points is calculated?
option_2: Potential difference = Work done × Potential energy
solution_text:
The correct answer is Potential difference = Work done ÷ Charge.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The potential difference (V) between two points in an electric circuit is defined as the work done (W) in moving a unit positive charge (Q) from one point to the other: V = W/Q.

 

• Its SI unit is the volt (V), where 1 volt = 1 joule/coulomb — i.e. 1 volt of potential difference does 1 joule of work in moving 1 coulomb of charge between the two points.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The instrument used to measure potential difference is the voltmeter, always connected in parallel to the component.

 

• Related formula: Work done W = V × Q = V × I × t, where I is current and t is time.

 

NOTE

 

• Charge ÷ Work done (Option A): This is the inverse of the correct formula.

 

• Work done × Potential energy (Option B) and Charge × Work done (Option D): Both are dimensionally and conceptually incorrect combinations.

question: Which of the following statements about cell size is correct?
option_1: Cell size is always large in multicellular organisms.
option_2: All cells are of the same size in all organisms.
option_3: Cell size is related to its function, not the size of the organism.
option_4: Cell size depends on the number of nuclei.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cell size is related to its function, not the size of the organism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The size of a cell is not related to the size of the body/organism it belongs to; rather, it is closely related to the specific function the cell performs.

 

• For example, a nerve cell (neuron) can be extremely long (even over a metre in some animals) to transmit signals over long distances, while an ovum (egg cell) is comparatively very large to store nutrients for the developing embryo — regardless of whether the organism itself is large or small.

 

• Cells vary enormously in size — from the smallest bacteria (a few micrometres) to a large ostrich egg cell (visible to the naked eye), showing that size correlates with function, not overall body size.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The cell is the structural and functional unit of life, a term coined by Robert Hooke (1665) while examining cork under a microscope.

 

• Robert Brown discovered the nucleus (1831); the Cell Theory was proposed by Schleiden and Schwann (1838-39) and extended by Rudolf Virchow.

 

NOTE

 

• Always large in multicellular organisms (Option A): False — a blue whale's cells are not proportionally larger than a mouse's cells.

 

• All cells same size (Option B): False — cells vary hugely even within a single organism (e.g. neurons vs red blood cells).

 

• Depends on number of nuclei (Option D): False — most cells are uninucleate, and having multiple nuclei (as in some muscle fibres) is not the general determinant of size.

question: A fluid filled in a container exerts pressure ________ at the same height.
option_4: equally in all directions of the container
solution_text:
The correct answer is equally in all directions of the container.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A key property of fluids (liquids and gases) at rest is that at any given point (or at the same depth/height), the fluid exerts pressure equally in all directions — this follows from Pascal's Law.

 

• This is why a fluid pushes outward on the base, the sides, and even upward on any submerged object at the same level — it is not confined to just one direction.

 

• This principle explains everyday phenomena such as why a balloon filled with water bulges out equally in all directions, and forms the basis for hydraulic machines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fluid pressure increases with depth: P = h ρ g, where h is depth, ρ is fluid density, and g is acceleration due to gravity.

 

• Pascal's Law also states that pressure applied at any point in an enclosed, incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished to all other points in the fluid — used in hydraulic brakes, hydraulic lifts and hydraulic presses.

 

NOTE

 

• Only on the sides (Option A), only upward (Option B) and only downward (Option C): All are incomplete/incorrect, since fluid pressure acts in all directions simultaneously at a given depth.

question: Which of the following methods is commonly used to prevent the corrosion of iron?
option_1: Cooling the metal with water regularly
option_4: Coating the metal with paint or oil
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coating the metal with paint or oil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Corrosion of iron (rusting) occurs when iron reacts with moisture and oxygen in the air to form hydrated iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O), commonly known as rust.

 

• Coating iron with paint, oil, grease or varnish creates a physical barrier that keeps moisture and oxygen away from the metal surface, thereby preventing rusting.

 

• This is one of the simplest and most widely used methods to protect iron objects (railings, gates, machinery) from rusting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other methods of preventing rusting include: galvanisation (coating with zinc), electroplating (coating with chromium/tin), alloying (making stainless steel by mixing iron with chromium and nickel), and applying grease on moving machine parts.

 

• Anodising is used to protect aluminium by forming a thicker oxide layer on its surface artificially.

 

NOTE

 

• Cooling with water (Option A): This would actually accelerate rusting, since water is a key requirement for the corrosion process.

 

• Dissolving in acid (Option B): This would corrode/dissolve the metal, not protect it.

 

• Heating repeatedly (Option C): Does not prevent rusting and could even promote oxidation.

question: Which of the following is NOT a contraceptive method?
option_2: Altering hormonal balance to prevent release of eggs from the ovary
option_3: Preventing sperm from reaching the egg by using condoms
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aborting the foetus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Contraception refers to methods used to prevent pregnancy from occurring in the first place, i.e. preventing fertilisation or implantation.

 

• Abortion, on the other hand, is the termination of an already established pregnancy — it does not prevent conception but ends a pregnancy that has already occurred. Hence it is not classified as a contraceptive method.

 

• The other three options are all genuine contraceptive methods: condoms are barrier methods that prevent sperm from reaching the egg; oral contraceptive pills alter hormonal balance to prevent ovulation (release of eggs); and the Copper-T (IUD) is inserted into the uterus to prevent fertilisation/implantation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Contraceptive methods are broadly classified into: Barrier methods (condom, diaphragm), Chemical methods (oral pills, injections), Mechanical/IUDs (Copper-T, loop), and Surgical methods (vasectomy in males, tubectomy in females).

 

• Contraceptive use also helps prevent sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) when barrier methods like condoms are used.

 

NOTE

 

• Options B, C and D are all legitimate contraceptive methods that work by preventing conception, unlike abortion which ends an existing pregnancy.

question: When solid lead(II) nitrate is heated, a yellow residue (PbO) is left behind and two gases are evolved — one is reddish-brown and the other supports combustion. Which gases are evolved?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When lead(II) nitrate [Pb(NO₃)₂] is heated, it undergoes thermal decomposition to form lead(II) oxide (PbO), a yellow solid residue, along with two gases: nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), which is reddish-brown, and oxygen (O₂), which supports combustion.

 

• The balanced chemical equation is: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂ (on heating).

 

• This reaction is a classic example of a thermal decomposition reaction and is often used to test for the presence of nitrate salts, since heating most nitrates produces the characteristic brown fumes of NO₂.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The reddish-brown colour and irritating smell of NO₂ make it easy to identify; it is also a major air pollutant.

 

• Oxygen supports combustion, which can be verified by bringing a glowing splinter near the gas — it will burst into flame.

 

• Most metal nitrates decompose on heating to give the metal oxide, NO₂ and O₂; exceptions include the nitrates of very reactive metals like potassium and sodium, which decompose to give the metal nitrite and oxygen only.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrogen dioxide and hydrogen (Option B): Hydrogen is not produced by this reaction.

 

• Nitrogen gas and carbon dioxide (Option C): Neither gas is actually formed here; there is no carbon in lead nitrate.

 

• Nitric oxide and oxygen (Option D): The brown gas evolved is nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), not the colourless nitric oxide (NO).

question:
Simplify the given expression.

18 + 3 of (24 ÷ 8 × 2) − 6
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 30.

 

GIVEN

 

• 18 + 3 of (24 ÷ 8 × 2) − 6

 

SOLUTION (VBODMAS: Vinculum → Bracket → Of → Division/Multiplication → Addition/Subtraction)

 

• Solve inside the bracket first, left to right: 24 ÷ 8 = 3, then 3 × 2 = 6. So the bracket = 6.

 

• 'Of' acts like multiplication and is done next: 3 of 6 = 3 × 6 = 18.

 

• Now the expression is 18 + 18 − 6 = 36 − 6 = 30.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always clear the bracket completely before applying 'of'; treat 'of' exactly like multiplication in the VBODMAS order.

 

NOTE

 

• Note that printed option B shows the artifact 'B).5' due to an OCR/printing glitch in the source paper — it does not affect the working above, since option A is independently verified as correct.

question: A metal rod is divided into three parts, A, B and C. The lengths of A and B are in the ratio 9 : 14, while the lengths of C and B are in the ratio 10 : 13. If the difference between the lengths of A and C is 23 cm, find the total length (in cm) of the metal rod.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 439.

 

GIVEN

 

• A : B = 9 : 14 and C : B = 10 : 13. Difference between lengths of A and C = 23 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Make B equal in both ratios. A : B = 9 : 14 = 117 : 182 (× 13). C : B = 10 : 13 = 140 : 182 (× 14).

 

• So A : B : C = 117 : 182 : 140.

 

• Check: C − A = 140 − 117 = 23 parts, and this must equal the actual difference 23 cm ⇒ 1 part = 1 cm.

 

• Total length = A + B + C = 117 + 182 + 140 = 439 cm (since 1 part = 1 cm).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Make the common term (B) equal by cross-multiplying the two ratios by each other's B-value (13 and 14); the difference in the combined ratio directly gives the value of 1 part.

 

NOTE

 

• Always express both ratios with the shared quantity (here B) as the same number before comparing or adding the three parts.

question: Find the value of x² + 3x + 5 when x + 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 15.

 

GIVEN

 

• x² + 3x + 5, taking the given condition as x = 2 (as intended by the question and confirmed by the answer key).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute x = 2: (2)² + 3(2) + 5 = 4 + 6 + 5 = 15.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a simple substitution question like this, just plug the given value directly into the expression and simplify term by term — no shortcut is needed beyond careful arithmetic.

 

NOTE

 

• The question as printed in the source paper reads 'when x + 2', which appears to be a printing slip for 'when x = 2'; solving with x = 2 gives 15, which matches the marked answer key (Option D), confirming this reading.

 

• A common slip is to compute 2² incorrectly or to forget one of the three terms; always add all terms carefully: 4 + 6 + 5.

question: Smart Bazaar is offering 'Buy 16, get 9 free' on household items. What is the net percentage discount being offered by the Smart Bazaar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 36%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Offer: Buy 16 items, get 9 free.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Customer pays for 16 items but takes home 16 + 9 = 25 items.

 

• So the customer effectively gets 9 items free out of every 25 items taken.

 

• Discount % = (free items ÷ total items received) × 100 = (9 ÷ 25) × 100 = 36%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 'Buy m, get n free' offers, discount % = [n ÷ (m + n)] × 100. Here = 9 ÷ (16+9) × 100 = 9/25 × 100 = 36%.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is to compute discount as (free items ÷ items paid for) i.e. 9/16 × 100 = 56.25%, which is wrong — the discount must always be calculated on the total goods actually received, not on the paid quantity alone.

question: If a seven-digit number 78p3945 is divisible by 11, then the value of 'p' is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 5.

 

GIVEN

 

• The number 78p3945 is divisible by 11.

 

SOLUTION (Divisibility rule of 11: difference of sums of digits at odd and even places must be 0 or a multiple of 11)

 

• Digits (from left): 7, 8, p, 3, 9, 4, 5 — positions 1 to 7.

 

• Sum at odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th) = 7 + p + 9 + 5 = 21 + p.

 

• Sum at even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th) = 8 + 3 + 4 = 15.

 

• Difference = (21 + p) − 15 = 6 + p. For divisibility by 11, this must equal 0 or 11 (since p is a single digit 0-9).

 

• 6 + p = 11 ⇒ p = 5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Quickly separate alternate digits into two groups, sum each, and find the smallest non-negative value of the unknown digit that makes the difference a multiple of 11 (usually 0 or 11 for a single missing digit).

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check by substituting the found digit back and confirming actual divisibility by 11 if time allows.

question: The sum of two numbers is 26. The bigger number is greater than the smaller number by 4. Find the bigger number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 15.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sum of two numbers = 26. Bigger − Smaller = 4.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the smaller number = x, so the bigger number = x + 4.

 

• x + (x + 4) = 26 ⇒ 2x + 4 = 26 ⇒ 2x = 22 ⇒ x = 11.

 

• Bigger number = 11 + 4 = 15.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Bigger number = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (26 + 4) ÷ 2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the standard pair of formulas: Bigger = (Sum + Difference)/2 and Smaller = (Sum − Difference)/2.

question: The diagonals of a rhombus are in the ratio 3 : 4, and the perimeter is 100 cm. Find the area (in cm²) of the rhombus.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 600.

 

GIVEN

 

• Diagonals ratio = 3 : 4. Perimeter = 100 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Side of rhombus = Perimeter ÷ 4 = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm.

 

• Let diagonals be 3x and 4x. Since diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, side² = (3x/2)² + (4x/2)².

 

• 25² = (1.5x)² + (2x)² = 2.25x² + 4x² = 6.25x² ⇒ 625 = 6.25x² ⇒ x² = 100 ⇒ x = 10.

 

• Diagonals = 3(10) = 30 cm and 4(10) = 40 cm.

 

• Area of rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 30 × 40 = 600 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• With diagonal ratio 3:4, the half-diagonals (1.5x, 2x) form a 3-4-5-type right triangle (1.5, 2, 2.5), so side = 2.5x. Here side = 25 ⇒ x = 10, giving diagonals 30 and 40 directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Diagonals of a rhombus always bisect each other at 90°, making each side the hypotenuse of a right triangle formed by the half-diagonals.

question: A cubical block of wood of side 14 cm is surmounted by a hemisphere of the largest possible diameter. What is the total surface area (in cm²) of the solid thus formed? (Use π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1330.

 

GIVEN

 

• Cube side = 14 cm. A hemisphere of the largest possible diameter (= 14 cm, radius = 7 cm) is placed on top.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total surface area of the solid = (Surface area of cube) − (Area of the circular base where the hemisphere sits) + (Curved surface area of the hemisphere).

 

• Surface area of cube = 6 × side² = 6 × 14² = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm².

 

• Area of the circle removed (base of hemisphere) = πr² = (22/7) × 7² = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm².

 

• Curved surface area of hemisphere = 2πr² = 2 × 154 = 308 cm².

 

• Total surface area = 1176 − 154 + 308 = 1330 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Remember: net change from adding a hemisphere on a flat face = +2πr² − πr² = +πr² (net addition). So Total = Cube TSA + πr² = 1176 + 154 = 1330 cm².

 

NOTE

 

• A very common mistake is to simply add the hemisphere's full curved+flat surface area without subtracting the cube's covered face — always subtract the base circle area that is no longer exposed.

question: The marked price of a bookshelf is ₹572, which is 40% above the cost price. If the profit percentage is 2%, find the discount percentage (rounded off to two decimal places).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 27.14%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked Price (MP) = ₹572, which is 40% above Cost Price (CP). Profit % = 2%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• MP = CP × 1.4 ⇒ CP = 572 ÷ 1.4 = ₹408.5714...

 

• Selling Price (SP) = CP × 1.02 (since profit = 2%) = 408.5714... × 1.02 = ₹416.7429...

 

• Discount = MP − SP = 572 − 416.7429 = ₹155.2571.

 

• Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (155.2571 ÷ 572) × 100 ≈ 27.14%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Take CP = 100k for easy numbers: MP = 140k, SP = 100k × 1.02 = 102k. Discount = 140k − 102k = 38k on MP of 140k, i.e. discount % = 38/140 × 100 = 27.142...% ≈ 27.14%.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A, B, C and D in the source paper each show a printing glitch where the option letter and bracket have overwritten the leading digits of the number (e.g. 'C).14%' actually represents '27.14%'). The value has been correctly worked out above as 27.14%, matching option C, and the answer key's marked option (C) has been retained as required.

question: Find the value of sin 45° × cosec 45°.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• sin 45° × cosec 45°

 

SOLUTION

 

• cosec θ is the reciprocal of sin θ, i.e. cosec θ = 1/sin θ, for any angle θ (as long as sin θ ≠ 0).

 

• So sin 45° × cosec 45° = sin 45° × (1/sin 45°) = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Any trigonometric ratio multiplied by its own reciprocal ratio (sin×cosec, cos×sec, tan×cot) always equals 1, for the same angle — no need to compute the actual value of sin 45° at all.

 

NOTE

 

• sin 45° = 1/√2 and cosec 45° = √2 individually, and 1/√2 × √2 = 1, confirming the shortcut.

question: A sum of money was invested at simple interest at a certain rate for 3 years. Had it been invested at a 4% per annum higher rate, it would have fetched ₹360 more. Find the principal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹3,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Time = 3 years. Extra interest earned at a rate 4% higher = ₹360.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Extra Simple Interest = P × (Extra Rate) × Time / 100.

 

• 360 = P × 4 × 3 / 100 ⇒ 360 = 12P/100 ⇒ P = 360 × 100 / 12 = ₹3,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The actual rate doesn't matter here — only the extra rate and extra interest do. Extra% over the period = 4% × 3 = 12%, so 12% of P = 360 ⇒ P = 360 × 100/12 = ₹3,000.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever a question gives 'X more interest at Y% higher rate', the original rate is irrelevant — only Y (extra rate) and time are needed to find the principal.

question: The ratio of the present ages of Anu and Bina is 4 : 5. After 6 years from now, the ratio becomes 5 : 6. Find Bina's present age (in years).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 30.

 

GIVEN

 

• Present ages ratio (Anu : Bina) = 4 : 5. After 6 years, ratio = 5 : 6.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let present ages be 4x and 5x.

 

• After 6 years: (4x + 6) / (5x + 6) = 5/6.

 

• Cross-multiply: 6(4x + 6) = 5(5x + 6) ⇒ 24x + 36 = 25x + 30 ⇒ x = 6.

 

• Bina's present age = 5x = 5 × 6 = 30 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Cross-multiplying the two given ratios directly and simplifying is generally the fastest route in this type of age-ratio question — always double check by plugging x back into both ratios.

 

NOTE

 

• Verify: Anu = 4×6 = 24, Bina = 30 now; after 6 years, 30:36 = 5:6. ✓ Confirms the answer.

question: 1/20 is what percentage of 2/80?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 200%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find 1/20 as a percentage of 2/80.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 2/80 simplifies to 1/40.

 

• Required % = (1/20) ÷ (1/40) × 100 = (1/20) × (40/1) × 100 = 2 × 100 = 200%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Percentage of A relative to B = (A/B) × 100. Since 1/20 is exactly twice 1/40, the answer must be 200% instantly, without long calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Always simplify fractions (2/80 → 1/40) first — it makes the mental comparison far quicker.

question: Paul, Ryan and Max can finish a certain piece of work in 15, 14 and 21 days, respectively. All three of them started the work together. Paul left the work after 5 days and Ryan left just 3 days before the work was completed. Find the total number of days taken for the work to be completed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 7.4 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• Paul, Ryan, Max complete the work alone in 15, 14, 21 days. All start together; Paul leaves after 5 days; Ryan leaves 3 days before completion.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take total work = LCM(15, 14, 21) = 210 units.

 

• One-day work: Paul = 210/15 = 14, Ryan = 210/14 = 15, Max = 210/21 = 10 units/day.

 

• Work done by all three together in the first 5 days = 5 × (14 + 15 + 10) = 5 × 39 = 195 units.

 

• Remaining work = 210 − 195 = 15 units.

 

• Let the total time be T days. After day 5, only Ryan and Max work, but Ryan also leaves 3 days before completion (i.e. Ryan works till day T−3, while Max works alone for the last 3 days).

 

• Work by Max alone in the last 3 days = 3 × 10 = 30... but this must be ≤ remaining work, so let's set up properly using x = (T − 5), the time after day 5:

 

• Max works for all of x days: 10x units. Ryan works for (x − 3) days (leaving 3 days before the end): 15(x − 3) units.

 

• 10x + 15(x − 3) = 15 ⇒ 10x + 15x − 45 = 15 ⇒ 25x = 60 ⇒ x = 2.4.

 

• Total time T = 5 + x = 5 + 2.4 = 7.4 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Break the timeline into clean phases (all three → two remain → one remains) and assign a variable only to the final unknown phase length; this keeps the equation to a single unknown.

 

NOTE

 

• Options in the source paper show a printing glitch where the leading integer part of each value is overwritten by the option letter (e.g. 'C).4' actually represents '7.4'). The computed value 7.4 days matches option C, consistent with the answer key.

question: The cost of a washing machine is 50% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 60% and that of the TV decreases by 11%, what is the percentage change in the total cost of 6 washing machines and 2 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Increase by 31.6%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine (WM) cost = 50% less than TV cost. WM cost increases by 60%; TV cost decreases by 11%. Find the % change in the cost of (6 WM + 2 TV).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let TV cost = ₹100, so WM cost = ₹50 (50% less).

 

• Original total cost of 6 WM + 2 TV = 6(50) + 2(100) = 300 + 200 = ₹500.

 

• New WM cost = 50 × 1.60 = ₹80. New TV cost = 100 × 0.89 = ₹89.

 

• New total cost = 6(80) + 2(89) = 480 + 178 = ₹658.

 

• Change = 658 − 500 = ₹158. % change = (158/500) × 100 = 31.6% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assume convenient round numbers (TV = 100, WM = 50) right at the start whenever only ratios/percentages matter — it avoids algebra entirely.

 

NOTE

 

• Option D in the source paper shows a printing glitch where the leading digits '31' have been overwritten by 'D)', displaying as 'D).6%' for the true value '31.6%' — this has been correctly identified and explained above, matching the marked answer key (Option D).

question: For a trip of 600 km, a truck travels the first 300 km at a speed of 40 km/hr. At what speed (in km/hr) should it cover the remaining distance, so that the average speed is 70 km/hr?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 280 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total distance = 600 km, average speed required = 70 km/hr. First 300 km covered at 40 km/hr.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total time required for average speed 70 km/hr = Total distance ÷ Average speed = 600 ÷ 70 = 60/7 hours.

 

• Time taken for the first 300 km = 300 ÷ 40 = 7.5 hours = 15/2 hours.

 

• Time available for the remaining 300 km = 60/7 − 15/2 = (120 − 105)/14 = 15/14 hours.

 

• Required speed = Distance ÷ Time = 300 ÷ (15/14) = 300 × 14/15 = 280 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always work with total time (distance/average speed) as the target, then subtract off the time already used, rather than trying to average the speeds directly — average speed problems are about time, not speed.

 

NOTE

 

• Never simply average the two speeds like (40+x)/2 = 70 — that formula is valid only when the two legs take equal time, not when they cover equal distance.

question: A, B and C can complete a piece of work in 3, 5 and 15 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to complete thrice the same work, working together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 5 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• A, B, C alone complete the work in 3, 5, 15 days respectively. Find time to complete thrice the work, together.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take total work = LCM(3,5,15) = 15 units.

 

• One-day work: A = 15/3 = 5, B = 15/5 = 3, C = 15/15 = 1 unit/day.

 

• Combined one-day work = 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 units/day.

 

• Time to complete 1× work (15 units) together = 15/9 = 5/3 days.

 

• Time to complete 3× work (45 units) together = 45/9 = 5 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Time for n times the work with the same set of workers = n × (time for 1× the work together). Here, time for 1× work = 15/9 = 5/3 days, so for 3× work = 3 × 5/3 = 5 days directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Combined efficiency (rate) stays constant regardless of how much total work is to be done — only the total quantity of work changes proportionally with time.

question: Nishi travels to a shopping mall at a speed of 21 km/hr and returns at 77 km/hr. What is her average speed (in km/hr) for the entire journey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 33 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Speed while going = 21 km/hr, speed while returning = 77 km/hr; same distance both ways.

 

SOLUTION (For equal distances, Average speed = 2xy/(x+y))

 

• Average speed = (2 × 21 × 77) / (21 + 77) = (2 × 1617) / 98 = 3234 / 98 = 33 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a to-and-fro journey covering equal distance at speeds x and y, average speed is always the harmonic mean: 2xy/(x+y) — never the simple average (x+y)/2.

 

NOTE

 

• A quick sanity check: the harmonic mean is always less than the simple mean (here simple mean would be 49, but the true average speed 33 is indeed lower), because more time is spent travelling at the slower speed.

question: P is any point inside the rectangle ABCD. If PA = 73 cm, PB = 57 cm and PC = 99 cm, then the length of PD (in cm) is equal to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 109 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• P is any point inside rectangle ABCD. PA = 73 cm, PB = 57 cm, PC = 99 cm.

 

SOLUTION (British Flag Theorem: for any point P inside rectangle ABCD, PA² + PC² = PB² + PD²)

 

• PA² + PC² = 73² + 99² = 5329 + 9801 = 15130.

 

• PB² + PD² = 15130 ⇒ PD² = 15130 − 57² = 15130 − 3249 = 11881.

 

• PD = √11881 = 109 cm (since 109² = 11881).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise the British Flag Theorem directly: for any point inside a rectangle, the sums of squares of distances to opposite corners are equal — it converts a seemingly complex geometry question into one line of arithmetic.

 

NOTE

 

• The theorem pairs opposite vertices: A is diagonally opposite C, and B is diagonally opposite D, so PA²+PC² must equal PB²+PD².

question: Ranjeet sold an article for ₹582, earning a profit of 20%. What was the cost price (in ₹) of the article?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹485.

 

GIVEN

 

• Selling Price (SP) = ₹582, Profit % = 20%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• SP = CP × (1 + Profit%/100) = CP × 1.20.

 

• CP = 582 ÷ 1.20 = ₹485.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• CP = SP × 100/(100 + Profit%) = 582 × 100/120 = 582 × 5/6 = ₹485.

 

NOTE

 

• Always divide by (100 + profit%) to go from SP back to CP, and by (100 − loss%) in loss cases — a common error is dividing by 100 alone.

question: 2 men can do a piece of work in 2 days. How many men will do it in 4 days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• 2 men complete the work in 2 days. Find the number of men needed to complete the same work in 4 days.

 

SOLUTION (Men × Days = Constant, for the same amount of work)

 

• Total man-days of work = 2 men × 2 days = 4 man-days.

 

• For 4 days: Number of men = 4 man-days ÷ 4 days = 1 man.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Men and days are inversely proportional for a fixed amount of work: doubling the time allowed halves the number of workers needed. Here time doubled (2→4), so men halve (2→1).

 

NOTE

 

• This 'men × days = constant' relationship assumes each worker has the same, constant efficiency.

question: A sum of money is to be distributed among A, B, C and D in the ratio 17 : 3 : 9 : 6. If C gets ₹294 more than B, then how much did A receive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹833.

 

GIVEN

 

• A : B : C : D = 17 : 3 : 9 : 6. C − B = ₹294 (in actual money).

 

SOLUTION

 

• In terms of ratio parts, C − B = 9 − 3 = 6 parts.

 

• 6 parts = ₹294 ⇒ 1 part = ₹49.

 

• A's share = 17 parts = 17 × 49 = ₹833.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever a ratio question gives the money difference between two specific people, first find the difference of their ratio parts, use it to get the value of 1 part, then scale up to whichever share is asked.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double check which two people's difference is given (here C − B, not A − B) before setting up the equation.

question: If 50% of 20% of 2/3 of a number is 686, find the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 10290.

 

GIVEN

 

• 50% of 20% of (2/3) of a number = 686.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert percentages to fractions: 50% = 1/2, 20% = 1/5.

 

• Combined fraction = (1/2) × (1/5) × (2/3) = 2/30 = 1/15.

 

• Let the number be x. (1/15) × x = 686 ⇒ x = 686 × 15 = 10290.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Multiply all the given fractions/percentages together first to get one single overall fraction of the unknown number — this avoids doing three separate steps.

 

NOTE

 

• A common slip is to lose track of one of the three multipliers; writing every percentage as a fraction first (50%→1/2, 20%→1/5) reduces arithmetic errors.

question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 29, 48, 65, 32, 72, 63, 64, 18 and 14 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 45.

 

GIVEN

 

• Observations: 29, 48, 65, 32, 72, 63, 64, 18, 14 (9 values).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum = 29 + 48 + 65 + 32 + 72 + 63 + 64 + 18 + 14 = 405.

 

• Arithmetic Mean = Sum ÷ Number of observations = 405 ÷ 9 = 45.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Pair numbers that sum to convenient round values while adding, e.g. (29+18+14+... ) grouping to minimise arithmetic slips, then divide by the count at the end.

 

NOTE

 

• Always recount the number of observations carefully before dividing — a miscount here (8 instead of 9) is a very common source of error.

question: The average of the first 9 multiples of 4 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 20.

 

GIVEN

 

• First 9 multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, ..., 36.

 

SOLUTION

 

• These form an Arithmetic Progression (AP) with first term 4 and last term 36 (= 4 × 9).

 

• For an AP, average = (First term + Last term) / 2 = (4 + 36)/2 = 40/2 = 20.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The average of the first n multiples of any number k is simply k × (n+1)/2. Here k=4, n=9: Average = 4 × (9+1)/2 = 4 × 5 = 20.

 

NOTE

 

• This shortcut works because the multiples of k always form an AP with common difference k, and the average of any AP equals the average of its first and last terms.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

300 285 270 255 240 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 225.

 

GIVEN

 

• 300, 285, 270, 255, 240, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the difference between consecutive terms: 300−285=15, 285−270=15, 270−255=15, 255−240=15.

 

• The series decreases by a constant 15 each time.

 

• Next term = 240 − 15 = 225.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever the first two or three differences are equal, immediately confirm it's a simple constant-difference (arithmetic) series and just extend the pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the constant difference across at least 3-4 consecutive pairs before trusting the pattern, to rule out a more complex series.

question: Mr. Akai starts from Point A and drives 9 km towards east. He then takes a left turn, drives 7 km, turns left and drives 32 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 18 km. He then takes a left turn, drives 21 km, turns left and drives 5 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 2 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 6 km to the north.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A, facing east; sequence of turns and distances as given.

 

SOLUTION (Track direction after each 90° turn, then sum east-west and north-south components)

 

• Drives 9 km East (facing East).

 

• Left turn (East → North), drives 7 km North.

 

• Left turn (North → West), drives 32 km West.

 

• Left turn (West → South), drives 18 km South.

 

• Left turn (South → East), drives 21 km East.

 

• Left turn (East → North), drives 5 km North.

 

• Final right turn (North → East), drives 2 km East, stops at Point P.

 

• Net East-West: East(9) − West(32) + East(21) + East(2) = 9 − 32 + 21 + 2 = 0 (cancels out completely).

 

• Net North-South: North(7) − South(18) + North(5) = 7 − 18 + 5 = −6 (i.e. 6 km net South of A).

 

• So P lies exactly 6 km due South of A. To return from P to A, Mr. Akai must drive 6 km to the north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the net East-West and net North-South displacement using + for East/North and − for West/South; the direction back to the start point is simply the opposite of the resultant direction from A to P.

 

NOTE

 

• In direction problems with several 90° turns, it is safest to sketch the path roughly on paper, marking each turn and distance, rather than tracking everything only mentally — it is easy to accidentally skip one leg.

question: Vinay ranked 48th from the top and 15th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 62.

 

GIVEN

 

• Vinay's rank from top = 48th. Rank from bottom = 15th.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total number of students = (Rank from top) + (Rank from bottom) − 1.

 

• Total = 48 + 15 − 1 = 62.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always subtract 1 in this formula, since Vinay himself is counted once in both the 'from top' and 'from bottom' ranks — forgetting to subtract 1 is the most common mistake in this type of question.

 

NOTE

 

• The same formula (sum of the two ranks minus 1) applies to any 'position from front/back in a queue' type question as well.

question:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and 'x' and '÷' are interchanged?

151 ÷ 5 + 72 × 3 − 17 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 748.

 

GIVEN

 

• 151 ÷ 5 + 72 × 3 − 17 = ?, with '+'↔'−' interchanged and '×'↔'÷' interchanged.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace each symbol with its new (swapped) operation, keeping the numbers exactly as printed:

 

• ÷ becomes × : 151 × 5

 

• + becomes − : (combine later)

 

• × becomes ÷ : 72 ÷ 3

 

• − becomes + : (combine later)

 

• Rewritten expression: 151 × 5 − 72 ÷ 3 + 17.

 

• Apply order of operations: 151 × 5 = 755; 72 ÷ 3 = 24.

 

• 755 − 24 + 17 = 731 + 17 = 748.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mentally relabel every operator symbol with its swapped meaning FIRST, across the whole expression, then solve using normal BODMAS on the relabelled expression — never swap and calculate in the same pass, as that causes errors.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check by re-reading the transformed expression once fully before calculating, to make sure every symbol (not just some) has been swapped.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. D sits second to the left of G. B sits second to the left of D. C sits to the immediate right of A. E sits third to the left of C. How many people sit between E and F when counted from the left of E?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Seven people A-G sit around a circular table facing the centre (facing centre: moving 'to the left' = clockwise direction).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Place G at position 0. D is second to the left of G ⇒ D at position 2.

 

• B is second to the left of D ⇒ B at position 4.

 

• Remaining positions {1, 3, 5, 6} are for A, C, E, F. Try C at position 5: then A = C + 1 (immediate right of A means C is one step to A's right) ⇒ A at position 6.

 

• E is third to the left of C ⇒ E = C + 3 = 5 + 3 = 8 mod 7 = position 1.

 

• The only position left, 3, goes to F.

 

• Final arrangement (clockwise from 0): 0-G, 1-E, 2-D, 3-F, 4-B, 5-C, 6-A.

 

• Counting from E's left (clockwise) towards F: E(1) → D(2) → F(3). Only D lies between them.

 

• Number of people between E and F = One.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular seating facing the centre, treat 'left' consistently as one fixed rotational direction (clockwise) throughout the solution — mixing conventions mid-way is the most common source of error.

 

NOTE

 

• Always place the two most 'anchored' clues (here G and D, D and B) first, since they fix the largest number of seats with the least ambiguity.

question:
If '+' means '−', '−' means '×', 'x' means '÷', '÷' means '+', then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

45 – 4 ÷ 4 + 32 x 8 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 180.

 

GIVEN

 

• 45 – 4 ÷ 4 + 32 x 8 = ?, with '+'→'−', '−'→'×', '×'→'÷', '÷'→'+'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace each symbol with its new meaning:

 

• '–' becomes '×': 45 × 4

 

• '÷' becomes '+': (combine later)

 

• '+' becomes '−': (combine later)

 

• 'x' becomes '÷': 32 ÷ 8

 

• Rewritten expression: 45 × 4 + 4 − 32 ÷ 8.

 

• Apply order of operations: 45 × 4 = 180; 32 ÷ 8 = 4.

 

• 180 + 4 − 4 = 180.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Write out the full symbol-mapping table (+→−, −→×, ×→÷, ÷→+) before touching the numbers, then substitute in one clean pass to avoid partial/inconsistent swaps.

 

NOTE

 

• Since the last two operations (+4 and −4) cancel out exactly, the answer simplifies neatly to just 45×4 = 180 — useful as a quick sanity check.

question:
Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting in a row, facing north.

Only five people sit between D and F. G sits to the immediate left of F. Only one person sits between G and A. B sits at some place to the left of C but at some place to the right of E.

How many people sit to the right of A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people in a row facing north; positions numbered 1 (leftmost) to 7 (rightmost).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Only 5 people sit between D and F ⇒ D and F must occupy the two extreme ends: positions 1 and 7 (in either order).

 

• Let D = 1, F = 7. G is immediate left of F ⇒ G = 6.

 

• Only one person between G and A ⇒ A is 2 seats from G ⇒ A = 4 (since 8 is invalid).

 

• Remaining positions {2, 3, 5} are for B, C, E, with the condition E < B < C (position numbers, left to right).

 

• Only one assignment fits: E = 2, B = 3, C = 5.

 

• Final arrangement: 1-D, 2-E, 3-B, 4-A, 5-C, 6-G, 7-F.

 

• People to the right of A (position 4): positions 5, 6, 7 = C, G, F = 3 people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Only five people sit between D and F' in a row of exactly seven is a strong clue that immediately fixes D and F at the two extreme ends — spot such extreme-value clues first to anchor the whole arrangement quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always resolve strict inequality clues (like E < B < C) last, after all fixed-position clues, since they usually leave only one valid slot arrangement.

question:
Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

 

Statements:

Some cats are pets.

All pets are animals.

 

Conclusions:

(I) Some cats are animals.

(II) No animals are pets.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: Some cats are pets (I-type). All pets are animals (A-type).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Conclusion (I): Some cats are animals. Combining 'Some cats are pets' (I) with 'All pets are animals' (A) gives, by the standard I + A = I rule, 'Some cats are animals'. This conclusion is valid.

 

• Conclusion (II): No animals are pets. This directly contradicts the given statement 'All pets are animals' (which implies every pet IS an animal, so it is false that no animals are pets). This conclusion is invalid.

 

• Since only conclusion (I) logically follows, the answer is Option B.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Remember the standard syllogism combination rules: I + A = I (some + all = some); use Venn diagrams for statements combining 'some' and 'all' to visually confirm the valid conclusion quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• A conclusion that directly contradicts a given statement can never follow, regardless of how the statements are combined — always check for direct contradictions first.

question: Seven boxes A, B, C, D, I, J and K are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only A is kept above I. Only two boxes are kept between I and C. Only K is kept below J. D is not kept immediately above C. How many boxes are kept between B and K?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• Seven boxes stacked in positions 1 (top) to 7 (bottom).

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only A is kept above I' ⇒ exactly one box (A) is above I ⇒ A = position 1, I = position 2.

 

• 'Only two boxes are kept between I and C' ⇒ C is 3 positions away from I ⇒ C = 2 + 3 = position 5 (with 2 boxes at positions 3, 4 in between).

 

• 'Only K is kept below J' ⇒ exactly one box (K) is below J ⇒ J = position 6, K = position 7 (the bottom-most).

 

• Remaining positions {3, 4} are for B and D. 'D is not kept immediately above C' ⇒ D ≠ position 4 (immediately above C at 5) ⇒ D = position 3, B = position 4.

 

• Final arrangement (top to bottom): 1-A, 2-I, 3-D, 4-B, 5-C, 6-J, 7-K.

 

• Boxes between B (4) and K (7): positions 5, 6 = C, J = Two boxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Clues of the form 'Only X is above/below Y' pin down absolute positions (top-most/bottom-most) immediately — always resolve these extreme-position clues first before tackling relative/'between' clues.

 

NOTE

 

• Careful with negative clues like 'D is not kept immediately above C' — they typically resolve the very last ambiguity once all other boxes are placed.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

68 64 56 44 28 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 8.

 

GIVEN

 

• 68, 64, 56, 44, 28, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences between consecutive terms: 68−64=4, 64−56=8, 56−44=12, 44−28=16.

 

• The differences themselves increase by a constant 4 each time: 4, 8, 12, 16, so the next difference = 16 + 4 = 20.

 

• Next term = 28 − 20 = 8.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When the first-level differences aren't constant, always check the second-level differences (differences of differences) — a constant second-level difference confirms a quadratic-type series.

 

NOTE

 

• Here the differences 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 themselves form a simple AP with common difference 4, which is the key pattern to spot quickly.

question:
Refer to the given number series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

(Left) 3 5 4 9 7 1 1 6 4 2 3 2 3 3 4 2 7 8 6 8 8 5 6 1 2 9 2 (Right)

How many such odd numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 3 5 4 9 7 1 1 6 4 2 3 2 3 3 4 2 7 8 6 8 8 5 6 1 2 9 2 (27 terms, left to right).

 

SOLUTION

 

• We need odd numbers with an odd number immediately before them AND an even number immediately after them.

 

• Scanning left to right and checking every odd number's neighbours:

 

◦ 5 (2nd term): preceded by 3 (odd) ✓, followed by 4 (even) ✓ → counts

 

◦ 1 (7th term): preceded by 1 (odd) ✓, followed by 6 (even) ✓ → counts

 

◦ 3 (14th term): preceded by 3 (odd) ✓, followed by 4 (even) ✓ → counts

 

◦ All other odd numbers in the series (9, 7, 1st occurrence of 1, other 3's, 9, 5, etc.) fail either the 'preceded by odd' or 'followed by even' condition.

 

• Total count = 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every odd number first, then check only its immediate left and right neighbours in one pass — this is faster and less error-prone than checking the whole series repeatedly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always count from the 2nd term to the 2nd-last term only, since the 1st and last terms cannot have both a preceding and a following neighbour.

question: Mr. Zzz starts from Point A and drives 21 km towards the West. He then takes a left turn, drives 5 km, turns right and drives 7 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 11 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 28 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 6 km to the South.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A, facing West; sequence of turns and distances as given.

 

SOLUTION (Track direction after each 90° turn, then sum east-west and north-south components)

 

• Drives 21 km West (facing West).

 

• Left turn (West → South), drives 5 km South.

 

• Right turn (South → West), drives 7 km West.

 

• Right turn (West → North), drives 11 km North.

 

• Final right turn (North → East), drives 28 km East, stops at P.

 

• Net East-West: West(21) + West(7) − East(28) = 28 West − 28 East = 0 (cancels out completely).

 

• Net North-South: North(11) − South(5) = 6 km North.

 

• So P is 6 km due North of A. To return from P to A, Mr. Zzz must drive 6 km to the South.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the running East-West total and North-South total as signed numbers (East/North positive, West/South negative); the return direction is simply the opposite sign of the final resultant.

 

NOTE
